bacterial growth was not synchronized with PPP in all aquatic systems and that direct phytoplankton C dependency of heterotrophs was questionable.
the relationship between BP and phytoplankton PPP in aquatic systems is weak and that phytoplankton-derived organic C does not contribute to a large extent to BP.
the relationship between BP and PPP is not as strong as previously thought and that phytoplankton are not the main source of C for bacteria in the oceans.

bacteria in freshwaters and oceanic waters have a different relationship with phytoplankton.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the direct C dependency of heterotrophs on phytoplanktons is not a universal rule in aquatic systems.
phytoplankton C is not the major substrate for bacterial C demand in most aquatic systems.
phytoplankton-derived C was a major substrate only for bacteria in freshwaters with moderate PPP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between BP and PPP is not a general rule, but a consequence of the environmental conditions and the system type.
the relationship between PPP and BP is not as simple as previously assumed.
bacterial production is not necessarily linked to phytoplankton primary production, and the direct C dependency of heterotrophs on phytoplanktons is questionable.
